I've had games where I literally can't even fight people because this item makes me kill myself even just from the passive damage return slapping me for 200 damage on every crit. If it goes active, I instantly die if I don't prefire BKB to stop it.

[Ability](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Abilities "Abilities") Passive Affects Enemies [Damage](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Damage_Types "Damage Types") Reflected / Source [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/c/c9/Blade_Mail_Damage_Return_%28Passive%29_abilityicon_dota2_wikiasset.png/86px-Blade_Mail_Damage_Return_%28Passive%29_abilityicon_dota2_wikiasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/File:Blade_Mail_Damage_Return_(Passive)_abilityicon_dota2_wikiasset.png) [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/a/aa/Dota2_Passive_Overlay_icon_allmode.png/86px-Dota2_Passive_Overlay_icon_allmode.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/File:Dota2_Passive_Overlay_icon_allmode.png) Any attack targeted at the wielder harms the attacker for a fixed amount, plus a percentage of the attack damage dealt. Base Damage: 10 Attack Damage as Damage: 15% ###### Details - Only reacts on [attack damage](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Attack_damage "Attack damage"). Other sources of damage are ignored. - Returns incoming damage before all [manipulations](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Damage_manipulation "Damage manipulation"). However, damage manipulation on the enemy still affects the damage normally. - Reflected physical damage is affected by [damage block](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Damage_block "Damage block") as well. - The returned damage is always dealt right after the incoming damage. - Returned damage has the [no-reflection flag](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/No-reflection_flag "No-reflection flag"), preventing its damage from interacting with other sources of damage with the same flag. - Fully procs [on-damage effects](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/On-damage_effect "On-damage effect"), except those which have a minimum damage threshold (e.g. [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/d/d7/Visage_Gravekeeper%27s_Cloak_abilityicon_dota2_gameasset.png/21px-Visage_Gravekeeper%27s_Cloak_abilityicon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Visage "Visage")[Gravekeeper's Cloak](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Visage#Gravekeeper's_Cloak "Visage")). - The damage has the [no-spell-lifesteal flag](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/No-spell-lifesteal_flag "No-spell-lifesteal flag"), preventing its damage from utilising [spell lifesteal](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Spell_lifesteal "Spell lifesteal"). - The damage has the [no-spell-amplification flag](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/No-spell-amplification_flag "No-spell-amplification flag"), preventing its damage from being amplified with [spell damage amplification](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Spell_damage_amplification "Spell damage amplification"). - Returns damage back to the source. This means damage done by summons is reflected back to the summons, not to their owner. - Damage Return has a global range and affects units through the [Fog of War](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Fog_of_War "Fog of War") or [invisibility](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Invisibility "Invisibility"). - Does not work against [wards](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Wards "Wards"), [buildings](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Buildings "Buildings") and allied units. ### Damage Return \[ [edit](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/index.php?title=Blade_Mail&action=edit§ion=4 "Edit section: Damage Return")\] Damage Return [Link](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/0/09/Blade_Mail_Damage_Return_1_soundsample_dota2_wikiasset.mp3)[Link](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/2/2b/Blade_Mail_Damage_Return_2_soundsample_dota2_wikiasset.mp3) [![Does not pierce Debuff Immunity sources.](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/a/ab/Dota2_Debuff_immunity_symbol_allmode.png/21px-Dota2_Debuff_immunity_symbol_allmode.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Debuff_Immunity "Does not pierce Debuff Immunity sources.") Blade Mail Reflection: Returning damage to attacking units. ## Recommended Heroes \[ [edit](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/index.php?title=Blade_Mail&action=edit§ion=5 "Edit section: Recommended Heroes")\] [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/0/08/Axe_icon_dota2_gameasset.png/80px-Axe_icon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Axe "Axe") **[Axe](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Axe "Axe")** - If taking [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/5/5a/Axe_Counter_Helix_abilityicon_dota2_gameasset.png/21px-Axe_Counter_Helix_abilityicon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Axe "Axe")[Counter Helix](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Axe#Counter_Helix "Axe") damage was not enough of a punishment for attacking the Axe, then Blade Mail will make sane people cry. [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/8/8e/Bristleback_icon_dota2_gameasset.png/80px-Bristleback_icon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Bristleback "Bristleback") **[Bristleback](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Bristleback "Bristleback")** - A highly durable hero, his namesake [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/6/67/Bristleback_Bristleback_abilityicon_dota2_gameasset.png/21px-Bristleback_Bristleback_abilityicon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Bristleback "Bristleback")[Bristleback](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Bristleback#Bristleback "Bristleback") helps him last longer in teamfights. Combined with Blade Mail, this provides him a significant increase in both offense and defense. [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/6/6b/Clockwerk_icon_dota2_gameasset.png/80px-Clockwerk_icon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Clockwerk "Clockwerk") **[Clockwerk](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Clockwerk "Clockwerk")** - Similar to [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/e/ea/Axe_mapicon_dota2_gameasset.png/21px-Axe_mapicon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Axe "Axe")[Axe](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Axe "Axe") and [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/4/48/Legion_Commander_mapicon_dota2_gameasset.png/21px-Legion_Commander_mapicon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Legion_Commander "Legion Commander")[Legion Commander](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Legion_Commander "Legion Commander"), Clockwerk can stop heroes from running away from him and forces out engagements while continuously barraging the enemy with [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/b/b9/Clockwerk_Battery_Assault_abilityicon_dota2_gameasset.png/21px-Clockwerk_Battery_Assault_abilityicon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Clockwerk "Clockwerk")[Battery Assault](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Clockwerk#Battery_Assault "Clockwerk"). Having Blade Mail makes it so much worse for them as Clockwerk's high health pool makes it very unlikely that he will die first - Clockwerk also benefits from all the stats Blade Mail provides. - The extra armor is very vital as Clockwerk is otherwise short in armor - The extra attack damage let him hit harder with his right-click [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/c/cc/Elder_Titan_icon_dota2_gameasset.png/80px-Elder_Titan_icon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Elder_Titan "Elder Titan") **[Elder Titan](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Elder_Titan "Elder Titan")** - Pairs really well with [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/6/64/Elder_Titan_Natural_Order_abilityicon_dota2_gameasset.png/21px-Elder_Titan_Natural_Order_abilityicon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Elder_Titan "Elder Titan")[Natural Order](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Elder_Titan#Natural_Order "Elder Titan"). - Elder Titan loves to be in the middle of the fight. [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/4/4a/Enchantress_icon_dota2_gameasset.png/80px-Enchantress_icon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Enchantress "Enchantress") **[Enchantress](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Enchantress "Enchantress")** - She can heal up quickly and will slow any direct attacker thanks to her passive, forcing anyone to cast strong spells on her to deal significant damage only to get it reflected back at them. [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/f/f8/Spectre_icon_dota2_gameasset.png/80px-Spectre_icon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Spectre "Spectre") **[Spectre](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Spectre "Spectre")** - Already having a damage reflect ability [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/b/be/Spectre_Dispersion_abilityicon_dota2_gameasset.png/21px-Spectre_Dispersion_abilityicon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Spectre "Spectre")[Dispersion](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Spectre#Dispersion "Spectre") Spectre ensures no one touches her as long as blade barrier is active. [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/c/cc/Wraith_King_icon_dota2_gameasset.png/80px-Wraith_King_icon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Wraith_King "Wraith King") **[Wraith King](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Wraith_King "Wraith King")** - Enduring tons of damage Wraith King can have breathing space. ## Tips \[ [edit](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/index.php?title=Blade_Mail&action=edit§ion=6 "Edit section: Tips")\] - It is a powerful counter against [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/4/4e/Bloodthorn_itemicon_dota2_gameasset.png/20px-Bloodthorn_itemicon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Bloodthorn "Bloodthorn")[Bloodthorn](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Bloodthorn "Bloodthorn") and [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/3/3c/Silver_Edge_itemicon_dota2_gameasset.png/20px-Silver_Edge_itemicon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Silver_Edge "Silver Edge")[Silver Edge](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Silver_Edge "Silver Edge") to prevent enemies from attacking you while under the debuff. - Enemies with copious amounts of damage resistance or high health could very easily ignore Blade Mail's ability. Heroes like [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/1/18/Ursa_mapicon_dota2_gameasset.png/21px-Ursa_mapicon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Ursa "Ursa")[Ursa](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Ursa "Ursa"), [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/3/33/Spectre_mapicon_dota2_gameasset.png/21px-Spectre_mapicon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Spectre "Spectre")[Spectre](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Spectre "Spectre"), and [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/9/93/Abaddon_mapicon_dota2_gameasset.png/21px-Abaddon_mapicon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Abaddon "Abaddon")[Abaddon](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Abaddon "Abaddon") are good examples of said resistant heroes, as are items such as [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/e/ec/Pipe_of_Insight_itemicon_dota2_gameasset.png/20px-Pipe_of_Insight_itemicon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Pipe_of_Insight "Pipe of Insight")[Pipe of Insight](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Pipe_of_Insight "Pipe of Insight") or [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/2/2d/Heart_of_Tarrasque_itemicon_dota2_gameasset.png/20px-Heart_of_Tarrasque_itemicon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Heart_of_Tarrasque "Heart of Tarrasque")[Heart of Tarrasque](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Heart_of_Tarrasque "Heart of Tarrasque"). - It can be useful to get Blade Mail if you get outcarried, to counter the DPS and turn the enemy's damage against them. - Buy it as a counter if the opposing team has high damage (crits, nukes or attack speed) and have low health. If timed properly, some heroes can get killed just from their own damage. And even if you cannot do that, it could make the enemy hesitant to attack you for 5.5 seconds. - A good situation to use Blade Mail is if you're inflicted with a heavy damage over time ability. For example, you can kill (or severely damage) [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/1/12/Bloodseeker_mapicon_dota2_gameasset.png/21px-Bloodseeker_mapicon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Bloodseeker "Bloodseeker")[Bloodseeker](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Bloodseeker "Bloodseeker") by walking around with [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/2/21/Bloodseeker_Rupture_abilityicon_dota2_gameasset.png/21px-Bloodseeker_Rupture_abilityicon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Bloodseeker "Bloodseeker")[Rupture](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Bloodseeker#Rupture "Bloodseeker"), or [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/7/7e/Tinker_mapicon_dota2_gameasset.png/21px-Tinker_mapicon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Tinker "Tinker")[Tinker](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Tinker "Tinker") by staying under his [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/f/f1/Tinker_March_of_the_Machines_abilityicon_dota2_gameasset.png/21px-Tinker_March_of_the_Machines_abilityicon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Tinker "Tinker")[March of the Machines](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Tinker#March_of_the_Machines "Tinker"). However, do make sure that you yourself can take the damage you'll be receiving, else you'll just be helping the enemy instead. - The return damage is only dealt to the unit who attacks. Therefore, [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/a/ae/Techies_mapicon_dota2_gameasset.png/21px-Techies_mapicon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Techies "Techies")[Techies](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Techies "Techies")' mines, [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/5/55/Witch_Doctor_mapicon_dota2_gameasset.png/21px-Witch_Doctor_mapicon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Witch_Doctor "Witch Doctor")[Witch Doctor](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Witch_Doctor "Witch Doctor")'s [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/e/e4/Witch_Doctor_Death_Ward_abilityicon_dota2_gameasset.png/21px-Witch_Doctor_Death_Ward_abilityicon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Witch_Doctor "Witch Doctor")[Death Ward](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Witch_Doctor#Death_Ward "Witch Doctor") and [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/0/04/Shadow_Shaman_mapicon_dota2_gameasset.png/21px-Shadow_Shaman_mapicon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Shadow_Shaman "Shadow Shaman")[Shadow Shaman](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Shadow_Shaman "Shadow Shaman")'s [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/5/5c/Shadow_Shaman_Mass_Serpent_Ward_abilityicon_dota2_gameasset.png/21px-Shadow_Shaman_Mass_Serpent_Ward_abilityicon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Shadow_Shaman "Shadow Shaman")[Mass Serpent Ward](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Shadow_Shaman#Mass_Serpent_Ward "Shadow Shaman") won't affect their main hero as they are considered separate units. - Since the Blade Mail returns damage on the unit that attacks the owner, you can use [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/3/34/Book_of_the_Dead_itemicon_dota2_gameasset.png/20px-Book_of_the_Dead_itemicon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Book_of_the_Dead "Book of the Dead")[Book of the Dead](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Book_of_the_Dead "Book of the Dead") units to attack and the melee [Necronomicon Warrior](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Necronomicon_Warrior "Necronomicon Warrior") will die quicker to return 800 damage. - This is a commonly bought item for initiator heroes that can soak up some damage (commonly [Strength](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Strength "Strength") heroes), such as [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/f/ff/Clockwerk_mapicon_dota2_gameasset.png/21px-Clockwerk_mapicon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Clockwerk "Clockwerk")[Clockwerk](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Clockwerk "Clockwerk") or [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/8/85/Spirit_Breaker_mapicon_dota2_gameasset.png/21px-Spirit_Breaker_mapicon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Spirit_Breaker "Spirit Breaker")[Spirit Breaker](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Spirit_Breaker "Spirit Breaker"). - Blade Mail is less effective with [evasion](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Evasion "Evasion") and attack slow because it reduces the hits you receive, and thus the damage you can return. - It also loses effectiveness against enemies who can turn themselves or their allies invulnerable with abilities like [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/1/13/Puck_Phase_Shift_abilityicon_dota2_gameasset.png/21px-Puck_Phase_Shift_abilityicon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Puck "Puck")[Phase Shift](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Puck#Phase_Shift "Puck") or [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/b/bf/Outworld_Destroyer_Astral_Imprisonment_abilityicon_dota2_gameasset.png/21px-Outworld_Destroyer_Astral_Imprisonment_abilityicon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Outworld_Destroyer "Outworld Destroyer")[Astral Imprisonment](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Outworld_Destroyer#Astral_Imprisonment "Outworld Destroyer"), or with [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/2/2d/Eul%27s_Scepter_of_Divinity_itemicon_dota2_gameasset.png/20px-Eul%27s_Scepter_of_Divinity_itemicon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Eul%27s_Scepter_of_Divinity "Eul's Scepter of Divinity")[Eul's Scepter of Divinity](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Eul%27s_Scepter_of_Divinity "Eul's Scepter of Divinity"), as Blade Mail cannot damage invulnerable units. - It is an ultimate counter against heroes who rely on critical strikes such as [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/b/bb/Phantom_Assassin_mapicon_dota2_gameasset.png/21px-Phantom_Assassin_mapicon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Phantom_Assassin "Phantom Assassin")[Phantom Assassin](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Phantom_Assassin "Phantom Assassin"), [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/3/34/Bounty_Hunter_mapicon_dota2_gameasset.png/21px-Bounty_Hunter_mapicon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Bounty_Hunter "Bounty Hunter")[Bounty Hunter](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Bounty_Hunter "Bounty Hunter"), [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/5/54/Wraith_King_mapicon_dota2_gameasset.png/21px-Wraith_King_mapicon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Wraith_King "Wraith King")[Wraith King](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Wraith_King "Wraith King"), etc. Also against [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/6/6c/Crystalys_itemicon_dota2_gameasset.png/20px-Crystalys_itemicon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Crystalys "Crystalys")[Crystalys](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Crystalys "Crystalys") or its upgrade [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/1/11/Daedalus_itemicon_dota2_gameasset.png/20px-Daedalus_itemicon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Daedalus "Daedalus")[Daedalus](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Daedalus "Daedalus"). ### Items Synergy \[ [edit](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/index.php?title=Blade_Mail&action=edit§ion=7 "Edit section: Items Synergy")\] - [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/4/41/Shadow_Blade_itemicon_dota2_gameasset.png/20px-Shadow_Blade_itemicon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Shadow_Blade "Shadow Blade")[Shadow Blade](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Shadow_Blade "Shadow Blade"), [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/d/dc/Blink_Dagger_itemicon_dota2_gameasset.png/20px-Blink_Dagger_itemicon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Blink_Dagger "Blink Dagger")[Blink Dagger](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Blink_Dagger "Blink Dagger") and [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/b/b3/Force_Staff_itemicon_dota2_gameasset.png/20px-Force_Staff_itemicon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Force_Staff "Force Staff")[Force Staff](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Force_Staff "Force Staff"): these are good ganking and initiation items. - [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/6/6a/Mask_of_Madness_itemicon_dota2_gameasset.png/20px-Mask_of_Madness_itemicon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Mask_of_Madness "Mask of Madness")[Mask of Madness](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Mask_of_Madness "Mask of Madness"): will protect you from being attacked while under the debuff of the Mask of Madness. - [![](https://liquipedia.net/commons/images/thumb/e/e6/Crimson_Guard_itemicon_dota2_gameasset.png/20px-Crimson_Guard_itemicon_dota2_gameasset.png)](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Crimson_Guard "Crimson Guard")[Crimson Guard](https://liquipedia.net/dota2/Crimson_Guard "Crimson Guard"): gives you more armor and damage block, allowing to return more physical damage than you take, since it gets reflected before reductions. - # Guide to Hero Counters ## Thread Locked | | | |-|-| | | Yes | | | No | | | | |-|-| | [Permalink](https://www.dotafire.com/comment-link?comment_id=55034) |
[Quote](https://www.dotafire.com/edit-comment?quote_comment_id=55034) |
[PM](https://www.dotafire.com/pm?r=create&recipients[]=L0bstz0r) |
+Rep
by [L0bstz0r](https://www.dotafire.com/profile/l0bstz0r-20991)
»
January 14, 2014 3:31am |
[Report](https://www.dotafire.com/report?relation_type=Comment&relation_id=55034)
sry pal, but i dont think that a "counterlist" will work in dota 2 as it does in LoL. For sure there are mechanics that are weak / strong against other mechanics (for example true strike > evasion) but there are no direct Hero-Counters in dota2, as itemization can be used to counter almost every mechanic.
for instance:
invis < [![](https://www.dotafire.com/images/item/dust-of-appearance.png) Dust of Appearance](https://www.dotafire.com/dota-2/item/dust-of-appearance-40); [![](https://www.dotafire.com/images/item/necronomicon.png) Necronomicon](https://www.dotafire.com/dota-2/item/necronomicon-96)
mobility < [![](https://www.dotafire.com/images/item/scythe-of-vyse.png) Scythe of Vyse](https://www.dotafire.com/dota-2/item/scythe-of-vyse-121); [![](https://www.dotafire.com/images/item/orchid-malevolence.png) Orchid Malevolence](https://www.dotafire.com/dota-2/item/orchid-malevolence-99)
nuke / disable < [![](https://www.dotafire.com/images/item/linkens-sphere.png) Linken's Sphere](https://www.dotafire.com/dota-2/item/linkens-sphere-103); [![](https://www.dotafire.com/images/item/black-king-bar.png) Black King Bar](https://www.dotafire.com/dota-2/item/black-king-bar-107), [![](https://www.dotafire.com/images/item/pipe-of-insight.png) Pipe of Insight](https://www.dotafire.com/dota-2/item/pipe-of-insight-87)
evasion < [![](https://www.dotafire.com/images/item/monkey-king-bar.png) Monkey King Bar](https://www.dotafire.com/dota-2/item/monkey-king-bar-81)
physical Damage < well...armor or [![](https://www.dotafire.com/images/item/ghost-scepter.png) Ghost Scepter](https://www.dotafire.com/dota-2/item/ghost-scepter-46)
....etc etc
my point is, that there is no need for hero counters in dota 2, as most hero mechanics can simply be countered by items. | ![](https://www.dotafire.com/images/avatars/windrunner.png)
[L0bstz0r](https://www.dotafire.com/profile/l0bstz0r-20991)

There were already several guides about hero counters as I googled it but they were all drafts or not published. I've also discovered [dotahut.com](http://dotahut.com/) which presents this topic but it lacks even a single concise explanation why this hero counters that hero. This is one of the reason why I came in to this idea.
To give you a hint, this would be the guide looks like:
(This was written by me and a friend on Feb 2011 but was not posted in any dota forums.)
* * *
INTRODUCTION
In hero picking, I often pick heroes that would counter the opponent's heroes. I don't pick heroes just because they are strong. Having a line up that counters the opponent's main bread and butter won 90% of the time than just picking 'imbalanced heroes'.These are lists of some Counters for almost all Dota heroes. I wont say that these counters are the best. These are only suggestions on how you can counter heroes that you find hard to defeat. I'll be focusing on the heroes' skill disadvantage. Items, like BKB, linken, manta, etc, wont be considered. I will consider only some items that the heroes are really dependent upon like blink dagger for Earthshaker. But, the rest are heroes without defending items. These heroes are arranged alphabetically.
Abaddon, Lord of Avernus
Some Hero Counters for Abaddon:
1\. Axe - Before Abaddon can trigger his borrowed time, axe can finish him off with Culling Blade.
2\. Doom - Borrowed time wont be triggered while doomed
3\. Lina - Perfect timing can kill Abaddon without letting him use his borrowed time
4\. Lion - same reason with lina
5\. Viper - simply slow him while he's using his borrowed time then finish him after
7\. Heroes with hex, euls, or skadi
Aiushta - Enchantress
Some Hero Counters for Aiushta:
1\. Bane Elemental - uses magical damage for Aiushta, Untouchable wont affect Bane for he is not doing normal attaks. Thus, when Aiushta uses her heal(nature's attendant), sleep her first.
2\. Lion - Disable her before she got to use her heal
3\. Zeus - he can have constant damage to Aiushta without having problem with Untouchable. With Aiushta's low hp, Zeus wont have any problem.
4\. Lina - 1 combo, Aiushta's dead
5\. Tinker - Spam spells then rearm
Aggron Stonebreaker, Ogre Magi
Some Hero Counters for Aggron Stonebreaker:
1\. Omniknight - Repel serves a big problem for ogre magi
2\. Bradwarden - Multicast can't kill heroes with High HP.
3\. Necrolyte - Ogre Magi has high hp but with reaper, Necrolyte can kill him with ease.
4\. Medusa - Aside from high hp of strength heroes, Medusa has mana shield that will make her hp not affected by multicast that much.
5\. Nerubian Weaver - Weaver wont be killed by one multicast. After getting multicasted weaver can just use its time lapse and bring back its full hp.
6\. Heroes with Defiance
Akasha, Queen of Pain
Some Hero Counters for Akasha:
1\. Puck - silence wont make her blink or use her other skills making akasha vulnerable to death due to her low hp apparently.
2\. Crystal Maiden - bite wont allow her to blink more than 3 secs.
3\. Doom - Same reason with puck, silence.
4\. Blood Seeker - Akasha wont blink while ruptured. If she does, the damage would be fatal and seeker will find her apparently because of thirst. Silence, also thus serves big problem for Akasha.
5\. Lion - With lion's disabling ability, akasha will have a hard time escaping.
Anub'arak, Nerubian Assassin
Some Hero Counters for Anub'arak:
1\. Puck - Vendetta is useless if Puck auto-activated its Phase Shift
2\. Slardar - Invi heroes' worst nightmare
3\. Low intelligence heroes - after the nerf made to anub'arak, low intelligence heroes wont be much affected by mana burn.
Anub'seran, Nerubian Weaver
Some Hero Counters for Anub'seran:
1\. Lion - can finish anub'seran without letting him escape or use time lapse.
2\. Slardar - Can chase Anub'seran's quick move speed and using Amplify Damage, there's no escape for Anub'seran.
3\. Tiny - can finish Anub'seran in one combo
4\. Doom - Anub'seran can't use his survival mechanisms when doomed.
5\. Puck - silence and coil wont let him escape
Atropos, Bane Elemental
Some Hero Counters for Bane Elemental:
1\. Pugna - Bane Elemental needs a lot of mana and Pugna's ward can damage him a lot.
2\. Earthshaker - ES's long range of stun can waste his ulti
3\. Tidehunter - Levi can wake up anytime within the length of sleep
4\. Doom - will make an skill dependent, like bane, useless
5\. Puck - silence or coil can easily disable atropos and waste his fiend's grip
Azwraith, Phantom Lancer
Some Hero Counters for Azwraith:
1\. Slardar - AOE stun can detect who's real and amplify damage will make dopplewalk useless
2\. Earthshaker - illusions help Earthshaker do more damage
3\. Leshrak - Pulse Nova, Split earth, Lightning Storm are skills that can wipe out Azwraith illusions as well as him.
4\. Lina - AOE spells can wipe out illusions and Laguna can wipe him out of the game.
5\. Kunkka - can wipe out Azwraith's illusions having 3 skills that can do AOE, particularly his splash normal damage.
Balanar, Night Stalker
Some Hero Counters for Balanar:
1\. Ezalor - Use mana drain on Balanar. With his fast move speed, he'll drain out of mana in no time.
2\. Axe - has high hp and wont die of spamming void. Axe's counter helix will give more damage to Balanar while attacking him.
3\. Bradwarden - Also a high hp hero. He wont die by spamming void. Attacking him will give more damage to Balanar too.
4\. Necrolyte - Though he may be silenced, the silence duration wont make him die. Thus, Balanar's high hp is countered by Reaper's Scythe.
Banehallow, Lycanthrope
Some Hero Counters for Banehallow:
1\. Strygwyr - rupture his 522 move speed.
2\. Enigma - he can't escape from black hole
3\. Rasta - shackles him to death
4\. Bane Elemental - Grip him to death. Use enfeeble to make his normal attack useless.
5\. Pugna - decrepify makes him or your allied heroes ghost and he wont be able to attack them.
6\. Ursa - can deal more damage than Balanar in one on one situation
7\. Ghost Scepter Heroes
Barathrum, Spiritbreaker
Some Hero Counters for Barathrum:
1\. Pugna - Decrepify makes his ulti useless
2\. Omniknight - Guardian Angel wont give you any damage too from his ulti
3\. Any stunner - will make him useless in team fights if perfectly executed.
4\. Necrolyte - strenght heroes' worst nightmare
5\. Ghost Scepter Heroes
Black Arachnia, Broodmother
Some Hero Counters for Black Arachnia:
1\. Dark Seer - ion shell and vacuum can both damage brood while inside the web. Surge when brood activates life steal. Dark seer makes brood mother a total trash.
2\. Slardar - makes web useless
3\. Earthshaker - has stronger ultimate because of the spiderlings
Boush, Tinker
Some Hero Counters for Boush:
1\. Balanar - Balanar can survive a lane against tinker. Silence can make tinker run. Void will make you catch him. Void can cancel travel.
2\. Doom - For silence purpose also, and canceling travel.
3\. Blood Seeker - For silence too
4\. Puck - For silence too and travel cancel. Dodge missile by using phase shift
Bone Clinkz, Bone Fletcher
Some Hero Counters for Bone Clinkz:
1\. Slardar - makes windwalk useless
2\. Pugna - Bone Clinkz is dependent on making normal attack for damage. Decrepify will make him do 0 damage for certain period of time.
3\. Lion - Disable Bone Clinkz to death.
4\. Ghost Scepter Heroes
Bradwarden, Centaur Warchief
Some Hero Counters for Bradwarden:
1\. Necrolyte - Reaper for his High HP.
2\. Venomancer - slowing him wont make him use dagger, it wont make him catch his opponent for stomp or double edge. Poison Nova eats his hp because the damage dealt is by hp percentage.
3\. Viper - Brad can't touch viper because of massive slow.
Chen, Holy Knight
Some Hero Counters for Chen:
1\. Earthshaker - Chen's creeps add to Echo Slam's damage.
2\. Kunkka - With kunkka's massive AOE, Chen's creeps will be gone in no time.
3\. POTM - Ganking heroes with escape mechanisms are quite difficult for chen.
4\. Doom - Devour chen's creeps.
5\. Enchantress - Enchant Chen's creep to have it your own.
Crixalis, Sand King
Some Hero Counters for Crixalis:
1\. Silencer - Epicenter can easily be canceled by Silencer wherever silencer is. Furthermore, silencer's last word makes crixalis's impale epicenter combo impossible to be done.
2\. Venge - Stun can cancel epicenter. Epicenter casted or not can be swapped away.
3\. Lion - has disable for epicenter and ground stun for sand storm.
4\. Batrider - Impale wont hit batrider while on firefly. Firefly does great damage making sandking run instead of using his sand storm. Flaming lasso also cancels epicenter.
5\. Puck - silence cancels epicenter. Phase shift can dodge impale or epicenter.
Darchrow, Enigma
Some Hero Counters for Darchrow:
1\. Silencer - Notrom can cancel his Black Hole anytime and anywhere as long as global silence is not on cool down. Last word wastes Black hole too.
2\. Puck - silence or coil can cancel Black Hole. Be sure to use waning rift behind enigma for you not to be joining the Black Hole party.
3\. Venge - Swap having long range can stop black hole anytime though Enigma has BKB.
4\. Doom - cancels Black hole though Enigma activated BKB.
5\. Earthshaker - Echo Slam will deal more damage because of Eilodons
Darkterror, Faceless Void
Some Hero Counters for Darkterror:
1\. Omniknight - Guardian Angel makes Chrono Sphere useless for Darkterror. He can't damage anyone because he only relies on normal attack to deal damage.
2\. Naga Siren - Sleep everyone after void used his Chrono Sphere.
3\. Vengeful Spirit - Swap void away from Chronosphere to lessen the time he can attack freely.

# Blade Mail – Dota 2 Guide, Stats & Hero Matchups \[Patch 7.41d\]

![](https://game.dotacoach.gg/vpk/panorama/images/items/blade_mail.webp)

[Upgraded Item](https://dotacoach.gg/en/items#upgraded-items) \| [Armor](https://dotacoach.gg/en/items#armor)

![](https://cdn-strapi.dotacoach.gg/1/31/main_shop_8c5a3cbbae.png)

Main shop

![Gold is the currency used to buy items or instantly revive your hero in Dota 2.](https://game.dotacoach.gg/vpk/panorama/images/hud/reborn/gold_small.webp)2400

A razor-sharp coat of mail, it is the choice of selfless martyrs in combat.

A hero's reflective shield, an ingenious and tactical item that not only protects your hero but also turns enemy damage against them in the most daring cost.

## Base Combat Stats

![bonus damage](https://cdn-strapi.dotacoach.gg/1/30/damage_large_8f016b30d4.png)

\+ **15** Damage

\+ **7** Armor

## Recipe

![](https://game.dotacoach.gg/vpk/panorama/images/items/blade_mail.webp)

[![](https://game.dotacoach.gg/vpk/panorama/images/items/broadsword.webp)](https://dotacoach.gg/en/items/broadsword)

[![](https://game.dotacoach.gg/vpk/panorama/images/items/splintmail.webp)](https://dotacoach.gg/en/items/splintmail)

[![](https://cdn-strapi.dotacoach.gg/recipe_blade_mail_cebca110e5.webp)](https://dotacoach.gg/en/items/blade-mail-recipe)

## Abilities

### Active: Damage Return

For **5.5** seconds, return all incoming damage, increasing the percentage by **85**%.

Mana: **25**

Cooldown: **25**

### Passive: Damage Return

Everytime you are attacked, you return **10** damage plus **15**% of the attack damage dealt to you.

## Additional Insights

- Damage Return is calculated before any kind of reduction.
- Returned damage type is the same as it was received.
- Damage done by this item is considered reflected damage. Reflected damage does not provide any lifesteal and cannot be reflected.
- Does not interrupts channeling when activating.
- Offering a defensive option that doubles as an offensive tactic. It's particularly effective when activated at the right moment during engagements, deterring enemies from targeting your hero or punishing them for doing so.

## Statistics

The statistics below shows the percentage of hero builds which contain Blade Mail as a core, common or situational item for each role. These statistics are based on our [hero guides](https://dotacoach.gg/en/hero-builds-steam-guides).

## Itemization Strategy

Fist Fight! Yes you read that right this item is heavily favored by cores who are highly to be targeted to return more a significant ammount of damage as he fights through the opponents, Best for hereos like Axe and Legion Commander and only think off like that cause if it's not their specialy the cost is not worth going for.

### Heroes with Blade Mail as Core Item

[![ undefined](https://game.dotacoach.gg/vpk/panorama/images/heroes/npc_dota_hero_axe.webp)](https://dotacoach.gg/en/heroes/axe)

A core item that combines well with Berserker's Call. Allows you to accelerate your farming speed even further. It is especially strong against high DPS right clickers and uncontrollable high AoE damage, e.g. Eclipse, Diabolic Edict, etc.

[![ undefined](https://game.dotacoach.gg/vpk/panorama/images/heroes/npc_dota_hero_bloodseeker.webp)](https://dotacoach.gg/en/heroes/bloodseeker)

A core item against physical damage lineups to become tanky with armor and do massive damage to the Ruptured enemy hero if they try to fight back.

[![ undefined](https://game.dotacoach.gg/vpk/panorama/images/heroes/npc_dota_hero_kunkka.webp)](https://dotacoach.gg/en/heroes/kunkka)

A core item against heavy physical damage lineups to tank up with armor and use your high HP pool and Ghostship rum buff to reflect damage back to enemy heroes.

[![ undefined](https://game.dotacoach.gg/vpk/panorama/images/heroes/npc_dota_hero_furion.webp)](https://dotacoach.gg/en/heroes/natures-prophet)

A core item to use the tankiness gained from {spirit-vessel} or {essence-distiller} to reflect damage back to enemy heroes after you Teleport in the middle of fights.

[![ undefined](https://game.dotacoach.gg/vpk/panorama/images/heroes/npc_dota_hero_legion_commander.webp)](https://dotacoach.gg/en/heroes/legion-commander)

A core item to get you kills with Duel and snowball in the game with the extra damage. Pop Blade Mail before starting your Duel with an enemy hero as you will not be able to use it during Duel. This will make them attack you and kill them during the duration of the Duel.

## Trivia

The concept and mechanics of Blade Mail have their origins in the original Defense of the Ancients (DotA) mod for Warcraft III. In DotA, Blade Mail was known as 'Return Damage', featuring similar mechanics where it reflected a portion of the damage taken by the hero back to the attacker for a duration.
